charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For State Bank of India: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For State Bank of India: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

deposits.title: Deposits and gross loans
deposits.content:
Deposits are the funding base; gross loans & advances are what the bank has lent out before provisions.

For State Bank of India: the ratio between the two (the credit-deposit ratio) shows how fully the deposit base is deployed into loans versus held in lower-yielding investments.

What to watch:

  • Loan growth outrunning deposit growth, which forces pricier wholesale funding
  • Both lines growing in step with nominal GDP, not materially faster (credit-quality risk) or slower (market-share loss)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For State Bank of India: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For State Bank of India: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For State Bank of India: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nim.title: Net interest margin
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income as a percentage of interest-earning assets.

For State Bank of India: the core profitability metric of a lender; a few basis points move earnings materially.

What to watch:

  • NIM trend with the rate cycle
  • Funding cost versus lending yield

assetQuality.title: Asset quality and provision coverage
assetQuality.content:
Gross NPA % is non-performing loans before provisions, as a share of gross advances; Net NPA % is after provisions. Provision coverage is provisions held as a share of gross NPAs.

For State Bank of India: as the country's largest lender by loan book, even a small percentage move in NPAs is a large absolute rupee swing; a rising coverage ratio with falling NPAs is the combination that de-risks the loan book fastest.

What to watch:

  • Gross/Net NPA trending down, not just coverage trending up
  • Coverage below ~70% leaves the bank exposed to a credit-cycle turn
  • Credit cost (impairment charge / advances) spiking ahead of NPA recognition

capitalAdequacy.title: Capital adequacy and CASA funding
capitalAdequacy.content:
CET1 and the Basel total capital ratio are regulatory solvency buffers against risk-weighted assets; the regulatory minimums are well below where SBI runs. CASA ratio is current + savings deposits as a share of total deposits -- SBI's cheapest, stickiest funding.

For State Bank of India: a high CASA ratio is the structural cost-of-funds advantage over private banks and a direct support for NIM; capital ratios set the ceiling on loan-book growth without a fresh capital raise.

What to watch:

  • CET1/Basel ratio drifting toward the regulatory floor as loan growth outpaces retained earnings
  • CASA ratio eroding as depositors chase higher term-deposit rates

returns.title: Return on equity and assets
returns.content:
ROE is net income over shareholders' equity; ROAA is net income over average total assets -- the two standard bank profitability yardsticks, reported annually here.

For State Bank of India: ROAA strips out the leverage a bank chooses to run, so it is the cleaner read on underlying earnings power; ROE is what the P/B-based valuation ultimately has to justify.

What to watch:

  • ROAA trend independent of leverage changes
  • ROE driven by margin and provisioning, not by rising leverage alone

costToIncome.title: Cost-to-income ratio
costToIncome.content:
Cost-to-income is operating expenses as a share of total income (net interest income plus non-interest income) -- a bank's operating efficiency measure, equivalent to an operating margin.

For State Bank of India: a large branch and employee network is both the distribution advantage behind the CASA franchise and a structural cost drag versus digital-first private banks; this ratio is the trade-off in one number.

What to watch:

  • Ratio trending down as digital channels take volume from branches
  • Spikes from wage settlements or pension provisioning, which are periodic, not secular

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For State Bank of India: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For State Bank of India: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For State Bank of India: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
